title: No time is no excuse
coreMove: Lack of time is often a disguised lack of priority; trade a few discretionary hours each week for protected work, and a side project moves from wish to evidence.

exampleSpecs.audience: would-be makers waiting to quit first
exampleSpecs.stakes: wait for a clean opening or start in the hours you already have
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist trades discretionary time for protected weekly work

exampleSpecs.domain: salaried employee building on the side
exampleSpecs.audience: people told to quit before they are serious
exampleSpecs.stakes: quit the job to seem committed or keep income while testing the idea
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist keeps the day job and starts in evenings and weekends

exampleSpecs.audience: makers waiting for one heroic marathon weekend
exampleSpecs.stakes: wait for a rare burst or let short sessions compound
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: small repeated sessions accumulate into a tangible result

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose dream stays an untested identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: name the real reason or keep the dream safely untested
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees the time excuse as a shield over desire

exampleSpecs.audience: people convinced their schedule is genuinely full
exampleSpecs.stakes: accept the no-time verdict or audit where the hours actually go
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist finds the shortage is a ranking, not an empty schedule

exampleSpecs.audience: people facing genuine survival or care constraints
exampleSpecs.stakes: apply the make-time pressure or recognize a real constraint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist distinguishes a genuine constraint from a discretionary one
